question: Can an untrained echo-state reservoir coupled to an incremental, label-conditioned Hebbian co-activation prototype readout classify images without backpropagation and degrade less under unseen common corruptions than linear-reservoir and gradient-trained baselines?

key_findings.claim: RECAP converts a static image into a relational population code and classifies it by overlap with class-specific binary prototypes.
key_findings.evidence: A constant normalized image drives a fixed leaky echo-state reservoir for 60 steps; states are time-averaged, uniformly quantized into eight levels, and expanded into a symmetric off-diagonal mask indicating which unit pairs occupy the same bin. Each class maintains a continuous pair matrix updated by additive potentiation on mask ones and multiplicative retention/decay on zeros; a top-density threshold produces a binary prototype, and inference chooses the largest Frobenius overlap.

key_findings.claim: The update is backpropagation-free but not label-free or purely two-factor local in the strong neurobiological sense.
key_findings.evidence: Only S^(c) for the ground-truth class c is updated. Thus every pairwise potentiation/decay event requires a class label and routing to one of C global prototype memories in addition to the states of units i and j. The paper appropriately restricts its biological-plausibility claim to local computation/plasticity, but the supervised class-gating signal is an important third factor and differentiates RECAP from unsupervised Hebbian or SOM readouts.

anchors.section: 2.3 Biological Plausibility and Local Learning Rules

key_findings.claim: The potentiation-decay state is highly presentation-order dependent, so the learned prototype is not simply a class co-activation frequency estimate.
key_findings.evidence: With eta+=0.6, two nearby positive events saturate a pair at one after clipping, whereas every subsequent negative event multiplies it by 0.96. Recent examples therefore have exponentially greater influence than early ones, and interleaving positives and negatives yields a different state from grouping them. The paper does not specify sample order, epochs, shuffle policy, convergence, or an order-sensitivity experiment.

key_findings.claim: The claimed approximately equal prototype density is not guaranteed under the stated quantile-and-greater-than-or-equal rule.
key_findings.evidence: The threshold is the (1-p) quantile and entries satisfying S_ij >= theta_c are retained. Because clipping, repeated multiplication by 0.96, symmetry, and identical histories create many ties, every entry tied at the quantile is included and density can exceed p=0.3 by an unspecified amount. Unequal realized densities would directly bias raw overlap scores toward denser classes; no achieved-density table, tie-breaking rule, or score normalization is reported.

key_findings.claim: On the reported MNIST-C protocol, RECAP has the lowest Relative mCE but pays a large clean-accuracy cost.
key_findings.evidence: Table 3 reports 34.1% Relative mCE for the proposed row versus 55.0% ESN-Ridge, 52.1% MLP, 99.9% ResNet-18, and 100% AlexNet. Clean errors are 11.7% for RECAP, 6.3% ESN-Ridge, 1.9% MLP, 0.9% ResNet-18, and 2.1% AlexNet. The authors explicitly frame the method as robustness-oriented rather than a replacement for optimized clean classifiers.

key_findings.claim: Relative mCE does not by itself establish superior absolute corruption accuracy because its numerator subtracts each model's clean error.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 14 averages (E_corrupt-E_clean) relative to AlexNet's degradation. RECAP starts at 11.7% clean error, so unchanged or mildly increased corruption error yields a small numerator compared with a 0.9%-error ResNet. The page-19 raw-error plots do show gentler degradation for many corruptions, but severe defocus, glass/motion blur, fog, contrast, and elastic transform still drive RECAP to roughly 50-85% error. The paper does not tabulate absolute mCE, average raw error, accuracy at each severity, or an accuracy-robustness Pareto comparison.

anchors.section: Appendix A Figure 6 full raw-error results

key_findings.claim: Noise and digital corruptions drive much of RECAP's Relative-mCE advantage; blur and some weather conditions remain difficult.
key_findings.evidence: Per-corruption Relative CE values for RECAP are Gaussian 10, shot 5, impulse 11, pixelate 5, and JPEG -15, while defocus/glass/motion/zoom are 49/56/72/27 and snow/frost/fog/brightness are 36/53/70/52. It equals MLP on motion blur (72), is only slightly better than ESN-Ridge on glass (56 versus 60), and remains far from zero degradation on fog and motion. This heterogeneous pattern is visible in both the main table and the full severity plots.

key_findings.claim: JPEG compression is a negative/null-style result in which average corrupted error is slightly below clean error for both reservoir readouts.
key_findings.evidence: JPEG Relative CE is -15 for RECAP and -13 for ESN-Ridge. The authors plausibly attribute this to compression suppressing high-frequency variation in simple MNIST digits and explicitly warn that it is dataset/preprocessing dependent rather than evidence that compression generally improves recognition.

key_findings.claim: The ESN-Ridge comparison supports a readout-level contribution but does not identify which RECAP component causes robustness.
key_findings.evidence: ESN-Ridge shares the same 1,024-unit reservoir and improves from 6.3% clean error to only 55.0% Relative mCE, whereas RECAP reaches 34.1% with 11.7% clean error. This isolates the whole readout pipeline from ridge regression, not discretization, pairwise equality, Hebbian dynamics, density thresholding, or overlap scoring individually. No continuous-feature prototype, non-Hebbian frequency prototype, nearest-centroid, random mask, K/p/eta sweep, or matched-clean-error ablation is reported despite the discussion attributing benefits to each stage.

anchors.section: Discretization, relational masks, and Hebbian prototype explanations

key_findings.claim: The pair representation is quadratic rather than compact at construction or inference time.
key_findings.evidence: For N_r=1,024, every sample mask and each continuous class state has 1,048,576 entries, even though symmetry means only half are unique. Ten class states contain about 10.5 million entries before binarization; naive training touches O(N_r^2) pairs per image and inference forms a full mask and scores C full matrices. Binary storage can be compact relative to floats, but no sparse implementation, memory footprint, operation count, training time, energy, or latency is given; p=0.3 is not especially sparse.

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence is a single controlled benchmark without the randomness and training detail needed to judge stability or baseline fairness.
key_findings.evidence: Only MNIST-C is used. No run count, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, reservoir/input-weight distributions, input scale, state initialization, preprocessing details, class/sample order, RECAP epoch count, validation selection, or corruption-independent hyperparameter tuning protocol is reported. ResNet-18 lacks optimizer/epoch details; AlexNet freezes all ImageNet convolutional layers and adds two transposed-convolution upsamplers; no modern corruption-training baseline is included. A particular random reservoir or tuning on MNIST-C could therefore account for part of the ordering.

key_findings.claim: The online and continual-learning benefits are architectural possibilities, not evaluated results.
key_findings.evidence: Updates are incremental and avoid backpropagation through time, so streaming use is plausible. The authors explicitly state that they do not evaluate continual-learning protocols, nonstationary streams, sequential tasks, catastrophic forgetting, or stability-plasticity tradeoffs. With global multiplicative decay and strong order dependence, those are central unanswered tests rather than minor extensions.

anchors.section: Implications for online and continual adaptation

key_findings.claim: The results tables retain the old label RC-HeCaP while the method and prose use RECAP, creating a reproducibility identity inconsistency.
key_findings.evidence: Tables 3 and 4 label the proposed row RC-HeCaP, whereas the title, equations, discussion, radar plot, and Appendix Figure 6 label it RECAP. The numerical row is evidently intended to be the proposed method, but no explanation of a rename or method-version equivalence is provided.

method.core_idea: Replace a trained linear reservoir readout with a class-conditional associative memory over quantized pairwise reservoir relations, using simple incremental potentiation and decay instead of error backpropagation.
method.mechanism: A normalized 28x28 image is flattened and repeatedly injected into a fixed sparse leaky ESN. The T=60 states are averaged; each of 1,024 unit averages is uniformly binned over [-1,1] into K=8 levels. A symmetric binary mask marks every off-diagonal unit pair sharing a level. For the labeled class only, mask-one entries receive +0.6 and clip at one, while mask-zero entries are multiplied by 0.96. After training, each class matrix is thresholded at its 70th percentile to target density p=0.3. A test mask is compared with every binary class matrix using unnormalized intersection count, and the maximum score is predicted.
assumptions: A random fixed reservoir with spectral radius 1.0, leak 0.5, and 90% sparsity supplies class-relevant and corruption-stable features without training.
Sixty repeated constant-input steps are sufficient to wash out transients and make the time average stable.
Uniform activation bins over [-1,1] are appropriately calibrated for every reservoir unit despite potentially different marginal state distributions.
Equality of quantized activation levels captures more class-stable information than reservoir magnitudes or linear combinations.
A ground-truth class-routing signal is available for every online update and is compatible with the intended locality claim.
The presentation-order-dependent potentiation/decay dynamics converge to useful class summaries under the unspecified sample schedule.
A quantile threshold with >= ties produces sufficiently equal class densities for raw overlap scores to be comparable.
Quadratic masks and prototypes can be stored and updated sparsely enough to remain practical beyond the 1,024-unit MNIST setting.
Relative mCE normalized to AlexNet and subtracting clean error adequately summarizes robustness despite different clean accuracies.
The one chosen random reservoir and reported hyperparameters are representative rather than selected on corrupted test performance.
MNIST-C behavior is informative about more complex images and natural common corruptions.

techniques.role: Maps a static image through untrained recurrent dynamics into a high-dimensional temporal population response.
Collapses 60 reservoir states into one vector and suppresses transient variation.
Discards small within-bin amplitude changes to form a perturbation-tolerant code.
Represents an input by which off-diagonal reservoir-unit pairs occupy the same quantization bin.
Adds 0.6 to active relations in the ground-truth class state and clips them at one.
Multiplies inactive relations by 0.96 so inconsistent pair relations fade.
Attempts to retain the top 30% of off-diagonal relation strengths in each class.
Classifies by the unnormalized count of relations shared by a test mask and each class template.
Tests zero-exposure corruption degradation over 15 corruption types and five severity levels.
Normalizes per-corruption degradation above clean error to an AlexNet reference.

limitations: Author-stated: the study is restricted to MNIST-C, and robustness may differ on complex natural images.
Author-stated: only natural/common corruptions are tested; adversarial robustness and broader domain shift remain open.
Author-stated: the model is bio-inspired rather than a faithful model of neurobiology.
Author-stated: exhaustive ablations of discretization levels, sparsity thresholds, and other hyperparameters are not performed.
Author-stated: N_r x N_r prototype matrices may require sparse implementations to scale.
Author-stated: online updates are not tested under sequential tasks, nonstationary data, or catastrophic-forgetting protocols.
Reviewer-inferred: the 11.7% clean error complicates Relative-mCE comparisons because the metric subtracts clean error; absolute mCE and Pareto-matched results are absent.
Reviewer-inferred: no seeds, variance, confidence intervals, significance tests, or reservoir-initialization sensitivity are reported.
Reviewer-inferred: reservoir/input initialization distributions, input scaling, initial state, sample order, epochs, validation protocol, and many baseline training details are missing.
Reviewer-inferred: only the whole readout is compared with ridge, so no evidence isolates quantization, pair relations, potentiation/decay, thresholding, or overlap scoring.
Reviewer-inferred: quantile ties can violate equal density, and raw overlap is not normalized for any remaining density or mask-cardinality differences.
Reviewer-inferred: the label-routed class update is a supervised third-factor rule; locality and biological plausibility should be stated with that qualification.
Reviewer-inferred: O(N_r^2) construction/update/inference, 30% prototype density, and full mask materialization conflict with the broad compactness/efficiency framing absent measured systems data.
Reviewer-inferred: the baseline suite omits modern corruption-robust training, nearest-centroid/associative-memory/HDC readouts, SOM/SoftHebb approaches, and clean-error-matched models.
Reviewer-inferred: use of an ImageNet-pretrained frozen-convolution AlexNet as the normalization reference and underspecified ResNet/MLP training makes fairness difficult to reproduce.
Reviewer-inferred: the proposed method is called RC-HeCaP in numerical tables and RECAP elsewhere, with no version-mapping explanation.
Reviewer-inferred: no code, generated MNIST-C artifact, corruption implementation hash, or exact raw-result table is linked in the paper.
failure_modes: A different reservoir seed can collapse class separation or shift state distributions across fixed uniform quantization bins.
Reservoir states concentrated in a few bins make equality masks dense and dominated by generic same-bin pairs rather than class structure.
Small changes near bin edges flip O(N_r) pair relations for one unit, undermining the intended perturbation tolerance.
Sequential ordering can erase an early stable relation through many later noncoactivations or saturate a recent relation after two positives.
Class imbalance gives different update counts and recency profiles, while per-class positive-only routing supplies no explicit negative-class competition.
Ties at the percentile threshold can yield unequal or unexpectedly dense prototypes and bias unnormalized overlap scores.
Two classes with similar broad reservoir-state histograms can share many equality relations even if discriminative magnitudes differ.
Quadratic pair construction and 30%-dense class templates can exhaust memory or dominate inference cost on larger reservoirs/classes.
High clean error can make Relative CE look favorable even when absolute corrupted accuracy is unusable.
Hyperparameters chosen after inspecting the MNIST-C test corruptions would invalidate the claimed unseen-corruption protocol; the selection procedure is not described.
Online adaptation to a shifted stream can catastrophically overwrite prototypes because every noncoactivated pair decays and there is no replay or consolidation.
JPEG or pixelation gains on MNIST can reverse on texture-rich natural images where high-frequency content is class-relevant.
The constant-input ESN may converge to a near-fixed point, making 60-step recurrence costly without adding useful temporal computation.
reusable_insights: A fixed reservoir is a useful controlled substrate for isolating readout design: compare multiple readouts on identical saved reservoir features and seeds.
Quantized relational codes can trade clean discrimination for perturbation stability, but stability should be measured directly as code flips versus input corruption.
Pairwise equality masks can be represented by K groups of unit indices rather than materialized N x N matrices; overlap may be computed from group intersections and upper-triangle counts.
Use an exponential moving frequency or analytically order-invariant count baseline to determine whether nonlinear saturation/decay adds value beyond class co-occurrence statistics.
Prototype density must be enforced with exact top-k tie-breaking or scores normalized by density/cardinality before cross-class overlap comparison.
Backpropagation-free, local-plasticity, label-free, online, and biologically plausible are distinct claims and should be audited separately.
Robustness reports should pair Relative mCE with clean error, absolute mCE, raw error by severity, area under the corruption curve, and a clean-accuracy-matched Pareto frontier.
A component-wise ablation ladder should include continuous state plus centroid, quantized vector plus centroid, equality mask plus frequency prototype, Hebbian dynamics without decay, and full RECAP.
Random-feature methods require seed distributions and reservoir/input-scale sensitivity because the untrained representation is part of the estimator.
Incremental update form is only a prerequisite for continual learning; stream order, class imbalance, drift, replay, and forgetting must be evaluated explicitly.
open_questions: How many reservoir seeds reproduce the 34.1% Relative mCE, and what is the confidence interval over seeds and sample orders?
Were eta+, eta-, K, p, T, spectral radius, and sparsity selected without access to MNIST-C test corruptions?
What exact input-weight/recurrent-weight distributions, scaling, state initialization, normalization, epoch count, and shuffle schedule were used?
What densities result after quantile ties, and does cosine/Jaccard/normalized overlap change class decisions?
Which stage causes robustness when continuous, quantized, relational, frequency-prototype, and potentiation-decay variants are compared at matched clean accuracy?
Can upper-triangle/group-count algorithms reduce construction and inference below O(N_r^2), and what are measured memory, latency, and energy?
Does recurrence add value over a fixed random feed-forward feature map or the reservoir's final state for static images?
How does RECAP compare with SoftHebb, LSM-SOM, OnlineHD, nearest class means, k-NN, and modern corruption-robust CNNs on the exact same split and metrics?
Do the Relative-mCE gains persist on CIFAR-10-C, ImageNet-C, real sensor corruptions, and domain shifts where textures and colors matter?
How does the label-gated update behave with imbalance, label noise, novel classes, and delayed labels?
Can a three-factor neuromodulatory interpretation make the supervised label routing biologically explicit rather than calling the update simply local Hebbian learning?
What happens under nonstationary streaming order, class-incremental tasks, recurrence of old classes, and catastrophic-forgetting evaluation?
Why do the result tables call the method RC-HeCaP, and are those numbers from the exact RECAP algorithm/equations in this version?

competitive_landscape.title: A Neural Architecture Search based Framework for Liquid State Machine Design
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct reservoir-design competitor evaluated on MNIST and other temporal or event-based tasks
competitive_landscape.difference: Tian et al. search a spiking liquid-state machine's multi-liquid architecture, neuron allocation, connectivity, and excitatory ratio with simulated annealing, obtaining 93.2% MNIST, 92.5% NMNIST, and 84% FSDD accuracy with 1,000 neurons and reporting 61.4% fewer connections than a single LSM. RECAP instead freezes a randomly drawn nonspiking ESN and learns a label-gated relational Hebbian prototype readout; its contribution is clean-trained MNIST-C robustness rather than dataset-specific reservoir optimization, but it provides neither comparable architecture/connection optimization nor a cross-task evaluation.
competitive_landscape.source_version: v1, submitted 2020-04-07; only arXiv version as checked

competitive_landscape.title: Large-scale spatiotemporal photonic reservoir computer for image classification
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct random-reservoir MNIST competitor emphasizing scalable physical implementation and a conventional trained readout
competitive_landscape.difference: Antonik et al. implement a 16,384-node photonic reservoir with randomly weighted input and hidden layers, engineered image features, linear-regression training, and winner-take-all decisions; their feedforward configuration reaches 1% MNIST error and recurrent dynamics are studied numerically. RECAP uses a smaller 1,024-unit software ESN and replaces regression with quadratic pair prototypes, yielding much worse 11.7% clean error but adding a clean-only-to-MNIST-C corruption test; it does not establish hardware scalability or isolate the value of its reservoir from its readout.
competitive_landscape.source_version: v1, submitted 2020-04-06; only arXiv version as checked; journal reference IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics 26(1), Jan.-Feb. 2020

competitive_landscape.title: SoftHebb: Bayesian Inference in Unsupervised Hebbian Soft Winner-Take-All Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct Hebbian image-learning and robustness competitor
competitive_landscape.difference: SoftHebb derives an unsupervised local online WTA rule as Bayesian inference/cross-entropy minimization and reports robustness to random noise and adversarial attacks as well as convergence behavior. RECAP instead applies a heuristic supervised potentiation-decay rule only at a reservoir readout and evaluates standardized common corruptions; it is simpler but provides no optimization theory, adversarial test, or direct SoftHebb comparison.
competitive_landscape.source_version: v4, revised 2022-11-12; first submitted 2021-07-12; Neuromorphic Computing and Engineering 2(4), 044017 (2022)

competitive_landscape.title: Hebbian Deep Learning Without Feedback
competitive_landscape.difference: Multilayer SoftHebb trains up to five feature layers without feedback, targets, or error signals and reports 99.4% MNIST, 80.3% CIFAR-10, 76.2% STL-10, and 27.3% ImageNet accuracy with an added linear classifier. RECAP leaves features random and learns only supervised class prototypes, giving lower clean accuracy but a specific MNIST-C common-corruption result and a directly incremental readout.
competitive_landscape.source_version: v2, revised 2023-08-02; first submitted 2022-09-23; ICLR 2023 published version

competitive_landscape.title: The Forward-Forward Algorithm: Some Preliminary Investigations
competitive_landscape.difference: Forward-Forward trains each layer with separate positive and negative forward passes and a layer-local goodness objective, eliminating the conventional backward pass while still learning representations. RECAP performs no representation learning and needs only positive labeled samples for class-prototype updates; it is more directly online at the readout but offers much less clean accuracy and no comparison with other non-backpropagation algorithms.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors present RECAP as a new bio-inspired strategy that couples untrained reservoir dynamics to a self-organizing Hebbian co-activation prototype readout, avoids gradient descent, supports incremental updates, and produces strong unseen-corruption robustness.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The concrete combination is an ESN time average, eight-level discretization, all-pairs equality mask, class-specific saturating potentiation/decay state, per-class density binarization, and overlap inference; on one clean-only MNIST-C experiment it reduces Relative mCE from 55.0% for the shared-reservoir ridge readout to 34.1%.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The exact relational-mask plus potentiation-decay packaging appears distinctive, and the shared-reservoir comparison makes it a useful preliminary readout hypothesis. The broader ingredients—fixed reservoirs, Hebbian/WTA or SOM readouts, class associative prototypes, quantization, and online updates—are mature and include closer operational precedents than the paper discusses. Novelty and practical value remain provisional because there is one benchmark/run record, no component ablation or matched-clean-error analysis, no direct local/prototype competitors, underspecified reproducibility, and an O(N_r^2) representation whose compactness and efficiency are not measured.

reviewer_notes: Complete primary pass over all 20 pages of arXiv:2603.06639. The source pin matches the current fulltext_index exactly. All extracted main-text pages, equations, tables, figures, references, and both appendices were read. The initially supplied extraction flagged PDF page 19 as missing text, so that landscape page was isolated and rendered at high resolution; its five raw clean/severity error charts and labels were inspected directly. The cache was subsequently OCR-refreshed and the provenance above pins that current 20/20-page extraction. PDF page 20's generative-AI declaration was also rendered and read. Main result tables on page 12 and method/hyperparameter tables on pages 10-11 were checked against rendered pages, resolving extraction artifacts: eta-=0.96 (not 0.9611), and the numerical tables really label the method RC-HeCaP. Current official arXiv metadata checked 2026-08-23 identifies v1, submitted 2026-02-25. Seven competitors were verified against current primary arXiv, ScienceDirect publisher, or IEEE proceedings records and enough primary abstract/body content to establish the stated relationship and difference. Approximate raw severity values are explicitly treated as visual readings because Appendix A is a chart rather than a numeric table. Confidence is high in the audit and reported numbers, but substantially lower in cross-dataset scalability and causal attribution because the paper supplies one underspecified experimental setting without uncertainty.
